messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High packet loss + BGP withdraws detected via upstream AS64512 from sfo-egress-1 probes. Sustained loss on ~12% of prefixes. Monitoring: https://mon.example.com/graph?m=upstream_loss
Ira: paging neteng + sre. I'm oncall for this window, assigning incident lead.
Sam: neteng here — seeing repeated route withdraws and rapid reannouncements from AS64512. AS path changes show prepends then withdraws. Likely provider-side instability.
Jin: prod-obsv: DNS query timeouts spiking in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 around the same time. Some customer-facing domains returning SERVFAIL intermittently.
Marcus: grabbing traceroutes now. traceroute -> 198.51.100.10 shows last hop into AS64512 then packet loss. Looks like egress blackholing on a subset of /24s.
Sam: confirming. This looks like provider egress jitter/partial blackhole, not our internal fabric. Contacting provider NOC now (ticket 78932).
Ira: mitigation plan: 1) fail traffic away from sfo-egress-1 to transit-2/bgp-2 2) reduce public DNS TTL for affected records to 10s 3) temporarily advertise more-specifics for affected prefixes if needed. Do we have bandwidth on transit-2?
Sam: transit-2 has capacity for reroute. I'll push route changes. Applying AS-path prepend on sfo-egress-1 to de-preference it while we shift traffic.
Sam: ```
router bgp 65001
 neighbor 203.0.113.5 route-map DEPREPEND out
 route-map DEPREPEND permit 10
  set as-path prepend 65001 65001 65001
```
Ira: ops-bot, run dnsctl to lower TTLs for affected zones: service.example.com, api.example.com
ops-bot: Command queued: `dnsctl update-ttl --zone example.com --record service --ttl 10`
ops-bot: Command queued: `dnsctl update-ttl --zone example.com --record api --ttl 10`
Kevin: support checking open tickets. Notified top 5 customers in EU and APAC. Drafting status page update: "Intermittent egress degradation via upstream provider affecting DNS and cross-region traffic. We're actively mitigating."
Maria: customer impact estimate: error rates up ~18% for EU read traffic, latency +200ms for some cross-region requests. Some memoizable CDN traffic unaffected.
Marcus: rolling routing changes now and watching convergence. BGP flaps reduced but still seeing sporadic withdraws for a few specific /24s.
Sam: provider replied: "we're investigating a partial hardware failure in our SFO POP, working on reroute. No planned maintenance." NOC ticket updated: 78932.
Ira: keep DNS TTL low until stable and retain prepends for 30m after no withdraws for 15m. Also enable per-route fallback to alternate model.
Marcus: metrics: packet loss on affected prefixes down from 12% to ~2% after reroute. DNS error rate down from 7% to 1.2%.
Kevin: status page posted and linked in CS slack. Customers acknowledged. No major data loss, primarily latency/timeouts.
incident-command: Handoff: Marcus (sre) will monitor for next 2 hours, Sam on neteng remains engaged for provider comms. Ira — thanks for coordinating.
Ira: oncall handoff noted. I'm updating the incident channel with a short playbook and creating a follow-up ticket to request provider RCA and BGP community filtering proof.
ops-bot: Incident timeline entry created: incident-2026-03-15-1799995000.
Marcus: temporary mitigation removed at 1799995200; leaving low-TTL until +30m. Continuing to monitor.
Sam: still seeing a couple of noisy prefixes; provider says they'll blackhole those internally until hardware fully recovered. We should expect some small fanning of errors for that subspace.
Ira: thanks everyone. We'll run a postmortem once provider RCA is available. If anything spikes, re-ping here or page oncall. :thumbsup:
